method: Same procedure as serenity's task 3 (as corrected 2026-08-22): for each compare spot, a horizontal landmark was named by eye in the photograph and the pitch=0 render (docs/superpowers/harnesses/2026-08-22-b4e/renders-pitch0-kings-court/), then measured at a chosen column with tools/pitch_fit.py --probe. Every landmark was visually confirmed by cropping both frames around the candidate row and checking they show the SAME physical object before any row was recorded -- the trap that cost serenity's task 3 two review rounds. Candidate degrees were rendered live in the browser (measure=1&fov=legacy=72, __measure()) and the same column re-probed; the chosen tilt is the swept value that MINIMISES the landmark-row disagreement, required to be an interior point of the swept range (confirmed here by widening past every initial coarse-round edge until the trend turned back up) and materially better than the 0deg disagreement -- no fixed tolerance (CORRECTED rule, see task-3-brief.md). sweptValues records the coarse round (0, proposal, proposal+-3, proposal+-6), any widening captures needed to turn an edge minimum into a confirmed interior one, and the +-1deg (or nearest-integer) refine around the located minimum. deg is the config pitch convention (positive = looking down). residualRows compares the confirmation-run row (docs/superpowers/harnesses/2026-08-22-b4e/renders-confirm-kings-court/, captured by loading the SHIPPED tour/apartments/kings-court.json directly under ?measure=1&fov=legacy with no per-spot JS override -- verified via currentCameraFov reading exactly 72 before capture) against the value the sweep itself measured at that same degree; all four tilt-confirmed spots reproduced EXACTLY (residualRows 0.0000).
coarseRoundDirsRef: docs/superpowers/harnesses/2026-08-22-b4e/round-{P,Pp3,Pm3,Pp6,Pm6}-kings-court/ (proposal, proposal+-3, proposal+-6, all 7 landmark-bearing spots captured together per round) and round-{W1,W2,W3,W4,W5,W6}-kings-court/ (widening and integer-refine captures, per-spot custom degrees, see each spot's sweptValues for which round supplied which point)
gateReadingRef: docs/superpowers/metrics/kings-court-b4e-task4.json -- taken against the SHIPPED config's own confirmation capture (renders-confirm-kings-court/), reproduced end to end: mean dE2000 (all-spot) 17.38, against BASE 17.56 (docs/superpowers/metrics/kings-court-b4e-BASE-legacy-allspots.json). Per rule, this number did not influence any tilt choice.

spots.landmark: the TV-wall media console's top edge (the low cabinet shelf under the TV where small objects sit)

sweptValues.phase: widen (round W1) -- worse than -4, confirms -4 is not an edge artefact
widen (round W2) -- confirms continued move away from -4

spots.reason: 0deg disagreement 0.0515. -4deg is a clean interior minimum: -3 (0.0164) and -5 (0.0086) both worse, and -7/-10 (0.0335/0.0731) confirm the trend turns back up well beyond -4, so the initial coarse-round edge at -4 is real, not truncated search. Residual after: 0.0032, inside bandRows -- essentially exact. Sign is negative (a slight upward correction), opposite the tool's small +2deg proposal.
spots.divider: At fov 98.2 and pitch -4, the render's left-to-right order matches the photograph's own (curtain wall, TV media wall, stair opening, dining table at the right edge -- see the spot's existing poseNote), and the corrected tilt lines the media console's top edge up closer to the photograph's. Furniture styling differs substantially (the render's sofa/console are much plainer and include an extra accent chair not in the photograph), a content difference already routed via the existing poseNote's meta.photoFovLong residual, not a pose one.

spots.landmark: the dining table's near surface (the line at plate/table-top height, visible as the row where cutlery and glassware sit)
spots.reason: 0deg disagreement 0.0494 is already far smaller than every coarse-round point -- disagreement grows monotonically and enormously (to 0.6194 at the tool's own neighbourhood) the moment any tilt is applied. The tool's 52deg proposal is a clear example of the documented unreliability (a near-flat dining-room table read as needing a huge downward tilt); the coarse round alone conclusively rules out that whole neighbourhood, so no negative-direction sweep was needed -- 0 is an interior minimum by a wide margin, not merely the least-bad edge.
spots.divider: At fov 98.2, the three hanging pendant lamps and the dining table's white top and chair arrangement broadly match the photograph's own composition and left-to-right order; the render's table setting (plates, glasses) is generic/placeholder compared to the photograph's styled table, a content difference, not a pose one.

spots.landmark: the ceiling-mounted range hood's bottom edge
spots.columnNote: render probed at column 0.80 -- the hood sits at a different horizontal position in the two frames' very different framings (see reason).

sweptValues.phase: widen (round W1) -- disagreement 0.0534, worse: the hood is exiting the top of frame and the candidate weakens
widen (round W2) -- hood fully off-frame, no candidate near its track

spots.precisionNote: The minimum is flat across 14.75-15.75 (disagreements 0.0081/0.0037/0.0080, all inside or barely outside bandRows of each other); 15 is the best-measured point and reproduced exactly in the confirmation capture, but the true minimum cannot be resolved much finer than +-1deg here.
spots.reason: 0deg disagreement 0.2032, the largest 0deg gap of any tilt-confirmed spot in this apartment. The hood is tracked continuously from level out to where it exits the top of frame past ~18deg (18.75 and 21.75 both confirm the object leaving frame, bounding the search from the high side). 15deg reduces the disagreement to 0.0037, inside bandRows.
spots.divider: At fov 98.2 and pitch 15, the hood sits near the top of frame in both the render and the photograph, consistent with the correction; the render additionally shows a dining table and sofa the photograph's tighter kitchen-only framing does not include, a framing difference expected at this fov per the brief.

spots.landmark: none could be confidently named in both frames
spots.reason: The photograph's strongest col-0.5 candidate (str 23.3, row 0.6696) is a crop-confirmed bed-cover/pillow fold -- furniture, and the render's row at the same position (str 5.7) is a crop-confirmed picture-frame edge on the wall: two different objects that happen to sit close in row, exactly the class of error the brief warns about. The photograph's dominant wall feature (a TV mounted beside a floor-to-ceiling shelf unit with a window) has no counterpart in the render at all, which instead shows a plain wall, a wardrobe and a tufted headboard the photograph's frame does not include. No shared architectural or even furniture-consistent line was found.
spots.divider: Not checked at the per-spot fov -- no landmark survived to a config change, and the mismatch is visible already at level: the two frames show materially different furniture layouts (TV+shelf+window in the photograph vs wardrobe+headboard in the render).

spots.reason: Carried in per the brief: this spot's ΔE noise floor is the worst in the apartment (0.32/0.30 against <=0.16 elsewhere) and the pre-flight's proposal (27.5deg on a two-run instability, 38.0deg on this run's own proposals file) is a documented example of the tool's unreliability. Crop-confirmed: the photograph's top candidate (row 0.1527, crown-molding/ceiling-line area near leopard-print wallpaper) and the render's candidate at the same row (a diagonal attic-roofline edge) are different feature TYPES (horizontal vs diagonal), not the same line. The photograph's desk, bookshelf and leopard-print wallpaper wall has no counterpart in the render, which shows curtains and a window instead.

spots.landmark: the bed's tufted headboard top edge

sweptValues.phase: widen (round W1) -- disagreement 0.0486, confirms 14 is not an edge artefact

spots.reason: 0deg disagreement 0.1454. The coarse round located an apparent minimum near 14 (0.0232), but 8 (0.0486, still better than 0) and the refine round showed 13 (0.0115) beating 14 -- so the true interior minimum is at 12 (0.0002, essentially exact), confirmed by 8 (0.0486) and 13 (0.0115) both being worse. Same physical feature (a dark blue tufted-panel headboard) crop-confirmed present and consistently shaped in both frames throughout.
spots.divider: At fov 98.2 and pitch 12, the headboard is visible on the right portion of the frame in both the photograph and the render, roughly matching relative composition; the render's much wider fov shows the wardrobe on the left that the photograph's tighter framing crops out, an expected framing difference per the brief, not a pose fault.

spots.renderRowAtZeroNote: weak (strength 6.0, against the photograph's 23.4) and not confidently the TV's own bottom edge rather than an adjacent wall-panel seam -- crop shows only a faint, low-contrast line at this row in the render.
spots.reason: The photograph's TV-bottom-edge candidate (col 0.28, strength 23.4) is clean and unambiguous by crop. No render-side candidate at any of eight tried columns reached comparable strength (max 8.0, most under 3) -- the render's TV sits against a low-contrast wall panel that does not produce a reliably trackable gradient, so no sweep could be built on it with any confidence. Not swept further given the weak starting candidate; matches serenity's own 3.webp, which independently reached the same no-usable-landmark outcome after a comparable multi-column search.

spots.landmark: the wall-mounted TV screen's bottom edge

sweptValues.phase: widen (round W1), opposite direction from the proposal -- disagreement 0.1548

spots.reason: 0deg disagreement 0.1163 -- the largest level-confirmed residual in this apartment, but genuinely the best reachable: disagreement grows monotonically in BOTH the proposal's own direction (positive, toward 27deg) and the opposite direction (negative, down to -9), so 0 is a true interior minimum, not merely untested elsewhere. Likely a TV-height/furniture-placement difference between the photograph's real television and the render's model, not a camera-pose fault this task can fix.
spots.divider: Not re-examined at the per-spot fov since the config is unchanged from before this task (pitch stays 0); the existing poseNote already documents the residual framing gap via meta.photoFovLong.

spots.columnNote: render probed at column 0.85 -- the sink sits at a different horizontal position in the two frames' very different wall styling (photograph: black/white marble; render: dark abstract-pattern wall).

sweptValues.phase: widen (round W4) -- disagreement 0.0505, worse: confirms 12.25 region is the minimum

spots.reason: 0deg disagreement 0.1489 (from the proposal+3 baseline) / the raw level disagreement is 0.1533 at renderRowAtZero. Disagreement fell monotonically as tilt increased throughout the entire -8.75..+18.25 range tested, with the minimum located at 12 (0.0065, close to bandRows) -- confirmed as interior by 9.25 (0.0272, worse) and 15.25 (0.0505, worse) both flanking it. Direction is opposite the tool's small negative proposal, consistent with this apartment's general pattern of unreliable proposals. Same physical feature (a round vessel sink's rim) crop-confirmed present in both frames despite the very different wall styling around it.
spots.divider: At fov 98.2 and pitch 12, the render's dark abstract shower wall sits on the left/centre and the white counter/sink sits on the right, matching the photograph's own left-to-right order (shower area left, sink/counter right) even though the tile styling itself differs completely -- a content/material difference, not a mirrored or rotated camera.
